<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**10** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (literal, 58 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e540baf8873c22642ce191b99e7e5ce1fd3b4620` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `613c15ade235b26fde7bfb47408521b67e98b7ab` — the merge of head `4cae1f45ab2246d254a51847b7bdd1e8a0752266` into base `e540baf8873c22642ce191b99e7e5ce1fd3b4620`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 613c15ade235b26fde7bfb47408521b67e98b7ab && git checkout 613c15ade235b26fde7bfb47408521b67e98b7ab
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e540baf8873c22642ce191b99e7e5ce1fd3b4620 4cae1f45ab2246d254a51847b7bdd1e8a0752266 && git checkout -B drift-repro e540baf8873c22642ce191b99e7e5ce1fd3b4620 && git merge --no-ff 4cae1f45ab2246d254a51847b7bdd1e8a0752266

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e540baf8873c22642ce191b99e7e5ce1fd3b4620
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `4cae1f45ab2246d254a51847b7bdd1e8a0752266`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Gate state on this head when it was read: 69 check-runs. 31 succeeded, 15 were skipped, 0 failed and 23 were still in progress (Test Core 8 of 8 shards, Test UI 14 shards, Type Check UI). Every Lint family had passed, and so had Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core and Type Check · workspace. This verdict judges the diff; the in-progress runs still have to finish green before the PR lands.

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff makes:
- **MCP `validate_expression` input schema.** It gains an optional input, `variables: z.array(FlowVariableSchema)`, which widens the accept set (under `strictToolInput` a call carrying this key was refused before). **Right.** The shape is the spec's own, imported from `@objectstack/spec/automation`, with no hand-written copy. A malformed variable is refused by the spec's strict object. One tool definition serves both doors through `wireBridgeTools`, and the stdio parity pin advertises the same `items.required` on both transports.
- **Off-site refusal.** `variables` at any site other than `flow_condition` is refused, in the same wording as `startCondition`, including an empty array at the default site. **Right.**
- **Without `variables`, answers are unchanged.** The probe, the hint and `gatePassFindings` each spread the key only when it is defined, so a call without the input builds the same probe and hint as on main; the CONTROL pins hold this. **Right.**
- **Validator half.** It receives the declared names through the existing `ExprSchemaHint.flowVariables`, read only at `scope: 'flattened'` (the flow_condition row of `VALIDATE_SITE_MAP`), the same key the gate hands the validator in `validate-expressions.ts`. The card's own scenario (`title * 2 > 10` with variable `title`) is pinned to the gate's verdict. **Right.**
- **Gate half.** `authoredFlowProbe` declares the variables, so the gate's own `warnShadowedFieldReads` reads them; nothing is re-implemented, and findings on the declarations themselves are dropped by `onSlot`. **Right.**
- **`@objectstack/lint` public type.** The exported `AuthoredSiteExpression` and `authoredFlowProbe` gain an optional `variables`: an additive type widening, named in the changeset. **Right.**
- **Description text.** The tool and input descriptions say the shadowed-read warning and the variable binding of a bare name need `variables`. **Right.**

Findings:
- nit: the spec-shape refusal test asserts only `isError: true`; the PR body and changeset say the refusal is the spec's own sentence, but no test checks the wording.
- nit: `FlowVariableSchema` comes in through a second `import` from `@objectstack/spec/automation`, beside the one that already imports `FLOW_TRIGGER_KINDS`.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset. Widening is correct (a new optional input on a closed tool schema, plus an optional key on an exported lint type); `packages/spec` is untouched and `FlowVariableSchema` is reused unchanged, so `none` is correct. A non-protocol widening ships `patch`: the changeset gives `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/lint` a patch, the two published packages the diff moves. **Matches.** Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none (dev report 6879320769).
- Input shape (the card left it open): an input rather than reading a named served flow. **Accepted** — reading a named flow needs a new bridge member on both doors and fails for an unsaved flow, the usual case while an agent authors one.
- Serial constraint with #33205: hunks in `authored-site-expression.test.ts` do not overlap, and this PR does not touch `validate-expressions.ts`. **Cleared.**
- `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` for the served SKILL.md line in `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts` and its Console mirror in `ui/apps/console/src/pages/developer/objectstack-skill.ts`: both list the `validate_expression` signature without `variables` (confirmed on main). should-fix, outside this diff's claim surface, **passed to the landing seat**: file the follow-up card and rewrite the line to `#N` before ACCEPT. It does not block this diff.
- Out-of-scope observation: given `variables`, the validator half receives only the declared names, while the gate on a real flow also leaves node ids, screen field names and the engine-bound names untyped. Pre-existing, disclosed in the Acceptance notes; the shadowed-read warning (declared variables only) is exact. **Accepted as noted.**
- Check-runs in progress (see ①): the landing seat arms only once they are green.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-33176-validate-expression-flow-variables`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5nhu4dRbKVQKDB4CDB`

**VERDICT: PASS**
